An edge not declared here fails the build.
cmd/ packages are the driving adapters. They are the only packages permitted to start a
goroutine and the only place dependencies are constructed, which is why cmd is absent
from noGoroutineSegments while domain and app are listed.

_comment_db: internal/db is the only package permitted to bind a transaction's isolation scope, per
TDD-organization-control-001. It has no internal edges on purpose: a package that could
reach a repository or a service could resolve a scope from something other than the
authenticated context, which is the substitution the RLS layer is a second line of
defence against. binding_test.go asserts the SQL side by walking the repository.
_comment_system: internal/system holds one constant: the CloudEvents source naming this system. It has no
internal edges and every publishing package depends on it, so the identity consumers key
their projections on is written once.
_comment_tenant: internal/tenant owns the Tenant state machine and tenant_security_version. It does not
import internal/membership and must not: TDD-organization-control-004 assigns the
offboarding freeze -- the one Tenant transition that touches Membership rows -- to
internal/offboarding, which will depend on both. An edge here would let a Tenant
transition suspend Memberships without the offboarding record that makes it resumable.
_comment_projection: internal/projection publishes the projection and reconciles it. It depends on neither
internal/membership nor internal/tenant: it reads the authoritative tables directly in one
database snapshot, because a snapshot assembled from service calls would be several
instants and could not carry a single high-water mark. An edge to either would also put a
mutation path within reach of a read-only publisher.
_comment_offboarding: internal/offboarding is the one package permitted to reach both internal/tenant and
internal/membership, because it owns the two Tenant transitions that also touch Membership
rows. TDD-organization-control-004 assigns the freeze here: entering offboarding stops
Tenant-wide access and then suspends every Membership in the Tenant, and a version of that
living in either of those packages would move one aggregate and leave the other.
_comment_context: internal/context is the authoritative fresh check. It reads the authoritative tables
directly and publishes nothing: a synchronous answer about now has no event to emit, and an
edge to internal/membership would put a mutation path behind a read that sits on the request
path of every high-risk operation in the estate.
_comment_registry: internal/organization and internal/workspace are the two remaining lifecycle aggregates.
Neither reaches internal/membership. Organization retirement and Workspace retirement are
both refused while something still references them, and both refusals read the referencing
rows directly: an edge would give a registry change a path to mutate the authority it is
only permitted to be blocked by.
_comment_invitation: internal/invitation reaches internal/membership because acceptance is the join: the
invitation state change and the Membership it produces must commit together, or an
accepted invitation exists that granted nothing. It does not reach internal/tenant --
the Tenant recheck is a status read inside the acceptance transaction, and an edge would
give the invitation flow a path to move a Tenant.
_comment_httpapi: internal/httpapi is the inbound transport. It reaches every service because it routes to
every service, and it reaches internal/db for one reason only: db.Scope, which it resolves
from the authenticated caller and places in the context. It holds no authority of its own --
no state machine, no statement, no policy decision -- so an edge in the other direction
would mean a domain package could answer an HTTP request, and no domain package declares
It does not import internal/controldb. Schema stage management belongs to the migrate
deployable, and a serving process that could advance a stage could do so on a request.
_comment_access: internal/access implements db.PrivilegedRecorder against audit.privileged_access. It
reaches internal/db for the interface and the Transactor type and nothing else: a recorder
that could reach a service could act on the access it is only supposed to witness.
It is imported by the composition root alone. No domain package depends on it, because none
should be able to write its own evidence.
_comment_config: internal/config reads the environment and has no internal edges. A configuration package
that could reach a domain package could validate a value by calling the thing it configures,
which is how a startup check becomes a database connection.
_comment_cmd_control: cmd/organization-control is the composition root: the only place the pools, the recorder,
and the ten services are constructed, and the only place net/http is used to serve. It
reaches internal/db because it builds both pools, and it reaches every service because it

github.com/jackc/pgx.reason: no package in this repository names the driver. foundation-platform's db package is the single place it is named, and every signature here carries db.Tx instead, so replacing the driver is one module's change rather than this repository's

database/sql.reason: the pgx pool in foundation-platform is the only connection source. a second one would open connections outside the transaction manager, and outbox.Append would no longer be atomic with the domain mutation it accompanies

net/http.reason: this service reaches no other domain over HTTP. ADR-ORG-001 5.4 gives it neither the Keycloak administration credential nor a network route to the kernel, and that prohibition is structural rather than procedural: an outbound HTTP client here would be the first step toward the projection path the Identity Control Service owns. The two packages excepted below serve; they do not call. An import-level rule cannot tell a server from a client once the package is excepted, so the prohibition that matters is enforced where it can be seen: internal/httpapi's outbound_test.go walks both packages for a client construction or a package-level request helper and fails on any. Widening this list without extending that walk would retire the rule while leaving it written down
